content:
Apple TV+ is currently streaming the fourth season of "Ted Lasso," with more highly anticipated series and films set to arrive on the streaming platform in the coming weeks. Below is the currently known Apple TV+ fall slate, which will be continuously updated as more premiere announcements are made.

September

Mayday

  • Release date: September 4
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Action comedy

Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh team up for "Mayday," a subversive, fast-paced buddy comedy that turns the spy thriller on its head. The story follows American Navy top pilot Lt. Troy "Assassin" Kelly (Reynolds), who during the height of the Cold War is sent on a top-secret mission into Russia that collapses, leaving him stranded behind enemy lines. Found by Nikolai Ustinov (Branagh), a rough-edged former KGB agent with a love of all things American, Troy assumes the worst — but an unlikely alliance between the two may provide a path to rescue and an unexpected friendship.

Last Seen

  • Release date: September 9
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Thriller mystery

Detective Ian Ridley (played by Patrick Baladi) hit rock bottom 11 years ago when his young daughter Maggie vanished without a trace. Now working as a police communications dispatcher, he is fueled by an unrelenting belief that she may still be alive. When he takes a call from a young woman in distress and is convinced she is Maggie, he will stop at nothing to find her and reunite his broken family.

Slow Horses Season 6

  • Release date: September 16
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Spy thriller

This darkly humorous espionage drama follows a team of British intelligence agents who, due to career-ending mistakes, have been banished to MI5's "slough house" — a dumping ground for agents whose careers have flatlined. Led by their brilliantly talented but irascible boss, the notorious Jackson Lamb (played by Academy Award winner Sir Gary Oldman), they navigate the smoke and mirrors of the espionage world in an effort to protect England from evil forces.

Brothers

  • Release date: September 23
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Comedy

"Brothers" follows semi-fictionalized versions of McConaughey and Harrelson whose longstanding friendship is thrown into chaos when they discover a long-buried secret: they might actually be blood brothers. After Woody's daughter's wedding falls apart, he brings his entire family to Austin to stay at Matthew's ranch for an extended stay. But when Matthew's mother, Ma Mac (played by Holland Taylor), lets slip the long-held secret that the two friends may be brothers, what was meant to be a healing getaway quickly spirals out of control. Woody turns the ranch upside down in search of the truth, while Matthew faces a separate identity crisis: a potential run for governor of Texas. The result is a heartwarming, chaotic and hilarious story about friendship, family, fame, and the blurry line between myth and reality.

October

The Last First: Winter K2

  • Release date: October 2
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Documentary

Directed by Amir Bar-Lev, "The Last First: Winter K2" dissects the extreme mountaineering industry and its shifting culture through a complex, thrilling, and emotional story. The film focuses on a 2021 expedition featuring Icelandic climber John Snorri Sigurjónsson and Pakistani father-and-son duo Ali and Sajid Sadpara, who set out to become the first to summit K2 in winter — when conditions are at their most punishing. They soon discover they are joined by influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and Nepali mountaineering legend Nims and his Sherpa team. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers up to K2's frozen peaks, through unpredictable weather, to reveal a surprising, layered story about strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power — all unfolding in life-or-death circumstances.

Matchbox The Movie

  • Release date: October 9
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Action

Based on the classic Mattel toy, "Matchbox The Movie" is a fast-paced, globe-trotting action adventure about a group of lifelong friends whose lives are upended when their former ringleader Sean (played by John Cena), an undercover CIA agent who vanished years ago, suddenly resurfaces in their small town — pulling them into a wild international chase and the mission to save the world.

Tenzing

  • Release date: October 16
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Drama

Based on a true story, "Tenzing" tells the little-known story of Tenzing Norgay (played by Genden Phuntsok), a gifted Himalayan mountaineer who, alongside New Zealand climber Edmund Hillary (played by Tom Hiddleston), became one of the first two people to reach the summit of Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (played by Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing wins the support of expedition secretary Jill Henderson (played by Caitríona Balfe). Together they convince Colonel John Hunt (played by Willem Dafoe) to allow Tenzing to join the British climbing expedition as a full member rather than as a porter for the support team. While Western climbers see "Everest" as a peak waiting to be conquered, Tenzing reveres "Chomolungma" as a sacred goddess mother. The climb that follows is fraught with tensions of background, class, and ambition, as well as the dangers of the mountain itself. But as they ascend above the world, empires, class, and ambition fall away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and for Tenzing, the dual fulfillment of a lifelong dream and spiritual calling. Directed by award-winning filmmaker Jennifer Peedom, "Tenzing" is a great story that refuses to be diminished — and the love that made that greatness possible.

Where's Wanda? Season 2

  • Release date: October 21
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Dark comedy

Apple's first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?" is a dark comedy about parents Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, who are desperately searching for their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda — who vanished months ago, a case police have failed to crack. The family decides to take matters into their own hands, securing surveillance equipment with help from their tech-savvy son Ole. Posing as utility company workers, they install listening devices around the neighborhood and across half the residential area, only to discover that their neighbors' true selves behind closed doors are nothing like their public personas.

Nocturne

  • Release date: October 30
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Crime drama

The series tells the story of Jonan Lynn (played by Liv Schreiber), a veteran-turned-homicide detective who is sick of the bloodshed on the streets of Philadelphia and decides to move to a small town in western Pennsylvania for a quieter life. But when the town and his family come under attack by a cunning serial killer, Jurek Walter (played by Graham), Jonah must do everything in his power to protect everything he holds dear. When the urgent search for Jurek's last missing victim forces Jonah to send his protégé — whom he regards as a son — FBI agent Saga Bauer (played by Beetz) — to confront Jurek head-on, just how far will Jonah be willing to go?

November

Being Heumann

  • Release date: November 13
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Drama

They wouldn't take Judy Heumann's phone calls, so she occupied their offices. In 1977, a young disabled woman (played by Ruth Madeley) and a ragtag group of outsiders finally had enough. What began as an impulsive act grew into the longest sit-in of a federal building in U.S. history — hundreds of people occupying government offices and refusing to leave until the bureaucrat (played by Mark Ruffalo) who had been blocking them took action. Bringing every form of rebellion into the hallowed halls of government, a group of unlikely leaders stumble down a road no one has walked before. Directed by Oscar winner Siân Heder (director of "CODA"), "Being Heumann" is based on a true story, telling the revolutionary, audacious, and profoundly human tale of a group of the most unlikely people attempting the seemingly impossible and changing millions of lives in the process.

Way of the Warrior Kid

  • Release date: November 25
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Action drama

For middle schooler Marc (played by Jude Hill), life at school is a nightmare — he's a good kid but gets bullied constantly, feeling behind in academics, sports, and friendships. Things take a turn when his injured Uncle Jake (played by Chris Pratt), a decorated Navy SEAL, comes to stay with Marc and his mom Sarah (played by Linda Cardellini) for the summer to recuperate. Determined to help Marc learn to protect himself, Jake devises a grand plan based on his SEAL training, codenamed "Operation Warrior Kid." Jake doesn't teach his nephew how to throw a punch; instead, he shows Marc what real courage looks like while facing his own demons. "Way of the Warrior Kid" is adapted from former SEAL Jocko Willink's bestselling novel, directed by McG (director of "Charlie's Angels" and "Terminator Salvation"), with a screenplay by Will Staples ("Without Remorse," "Call of Duty").

Apple is expected to announce more details about its fall titles in the coming weeks. But for now, that's everything that's been revealed.

Apple TV+ costs $12.99 per month, or you can subscribe via the Apple One bundle deal.
